items.stem: On 25 June 1950 North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel into South Korea. (a) Describe the main events of the Korean War from 1950 to 1953. [4] (b) Why did the USA become involved in the Korean War? [6]
items.answer: (a) North Korea invaded in June 1950 and pushed UN and South Korean forces back to Pusan. UN forces landed at Inchon in September 1950 and drove the North Koreans back. UN forces crossed the 38th parallel and advanced towards the Yalu River. China entered the war in October-November 1950 and pushed UN forces back south. The war became a stalemate near the 38th parallel until the armistice of July 1953. (b) Truman believed in containment and the domino theory. China had become communist in 1949 and the USA feared communism spreading across Asia. The USSR had tested an atomic bomb in 1949 and NSC-68 called for a stronger response. Truman faced criticism at home for “losing” China and needed to appear strong. A communist South Korea would threaten Japan.

items.stem: The Korean War was the first major conflict of the Cold War. Describe the role of the United Nations in the Korean War.
items.answer: The Security Council condemned the invasion and called on members to help South Korea. The USSR could not veto this because it was boycotting the Council. Sixteen countries sent troops, though most were American. The UN force was commanded by the American General MacArthur.

items.answer: For: South Korea remained non-communist. The UN, led by the USA, showed aggression would be resisted. The USA rearmed and strengthened alliances such as SEATO (1954). items.stem: For thirteen days in October 1962 the world seemed close to nuclear war. (a) Describe the events of the Cuban Missile Crisis from 14 to 28 October 1962. [4] (b) Why was the Cuban Missile Crisis resolved without war? [6]
items.answer: (a) A U-2 plane photographed missile sites in Cuba on 14 October. Kennedy and ExComm discussed options including an air strike and invasion. On 22 October Kennedy announced a naval quarantine of Cuba. Soviet ships carrying missiles turned back on 24 October. Khrushchev sent two letters on 26 and 27 October and a U-2 was shot down. On 28 October Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles. (b) Both leaders realised the danger of nuclear war. Kennedy chose a quarantine rather than an attack. Khrushchev accepted a deal: no US invasion of Cuba and, secretly, removal of the Jupiter missiles. Back-channel talks, such as Robert Kennedy's meeting with the Soviet ambassador, allowed compromise.

items.stem: ‘Kennedy won the Cuban Missile Crisis.’ How far do you agree? Explain your answer.
items.answer: For: The Soviet missiles were removed from Cuba. Kennedy appeared firm and his reputation rose. Khrushchev was humiliated and removed from power in 1964. Against: Khrushchev gained a promise that the USA would not invade Cuba, so Castro survived. The US Jupiter missiles were removed from Turkey. Both sides gained from the hotline and the Test Ban Treaty. Judgement: Kennedy appeared to win because the deal on Turkey was secret, but Khrushchev gained important concessions; in reality both sides gained by avoiding war.

items.stem: By the end of 1968 there were over half a million American troops in Vietnam. ‘The tactics of the Viet Cong were the main reason why the USA failed in Vietnam.’ How far do you agree? Explain your answer.
items.answer: For: Guerrilla warfare and tunnels neutralised American firepower. The Ho Chi Minh Trail kept them supplied. They won support from many villagers. Against: US tactics such as search and destroy alienated the population. The South Vietnamese government was corrupt and unpopular. Opposition grew in the USA, especially after Tet in 1968. North Vietnam received aid from China and the USSR. Judgement: Viet Cong tactics were crucial, but they succeeded because US methods and an unpopular South Vietnamese government made it impossible to win support.

items.stem: In October 1962 an American U-2 spy plane photographed Soviet missile sites under construction in Cuba. How far was the Cuban Missile Crisis a success for containment? Explain your answer.
items.answer: For: Soviet missiles were removed from the western hemisphere. The USA showed it would stand firm against Soviet expansion. Against: Cuba remained a communist state close to the USA. The USA had to promise not to invade Cuba. Containment had already failed in Cuba in 1959-61 with Castro's turn to the USSR. Judgement: The crisis contained the nuclear threat, but it confirmed rather than reversed communism in Cuba.

items.stem: In October 1962 an American U-2 spy plane photographed Soviet missile sites under construction in Cuba. (a) Describe the events of the Cuban Missile Crisis from 14 to 28 October 1962. [4] (b) ‘Kennedy won the Cuban Missile Crisis.’ How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer. [10]
items.answer: (a) A U-2 plane photographed missile sites in Cuba on 14 October. Kennedy and ExComm discussed options including an air strike and invasion. On 22 October Kennedy announced a naval quarantine of Cuba. Soviet ships carrying missiles turned back on 24 October. Khrushchev sent two letters on 26 and 27 October and a U-2 was shot down. On 28 October Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles. (b) For: The Soviet missiles were removed from Cuba. Kennedy appeared firm and his reputation rose. Khrushchev was humiliated and removed from power in 1964. Against: Khrushchev gained a promise that the USA would not invade Cuba, so Castro survived. The US Jupiter missiles were removed from Turkey. Both sides gained from the hotline and the Test Ban Treaty. Judgement: Kennedy appeared to win because the deal on Turkey was secret, but Khrushchev gained important concessions; in reality both sides gained by avoiding war.

items.stem: Describe the tactics used by the Viet Cong.
items.answer: They used guerrilla warfare, attacking in small groups and then disappearing. They used booby traps and mines. They hid in tunnel networks such as those at Cu Chi. They mixed with villagers, making them hard to identify. They were supplied along the Ho Chi Minh Trail.

items.stem: In 1954 the Geneva Agreements divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel. Describe how US involvement in Vietnam increased between 1954 and 1965.
items.answer: The USA supported Ngo Dinh Diem's government in South Vietnam after 1954. Eisenhower sent money and military advisers. Kennedy increased the number of advisers to about 16,000 by 1963. After the Gulf of Tonkin incident in 1964 Congress gave Johnson power to act. In 1965 Johnson began Operation Rolling Thunder and sent combat troops.

items.stem: On 25 June 1950 North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel into South Korea. How far was the USA responsible for the Korean War becoming a wider conflict? Explain your answer.
items.answer: For: UN forces crossed the 38th parallel and advanced to China's border at the Yalu. MacArthur ignored Chinese warnings. Against: North Korea began the war with Soviet approval. China chose to send hundreds of thousands of troops. Truman kept the war limited by refusing to use atomic bombs or attack China. Judgement: The decision to advance to the Yalu brought China in, but the USA also took steps to keep the war from spreading further.

items.stem: Why did Khrushchev place nuclear missiles on Cuba? Give one reason.
items.answer: To protect Cuba, a communist ally, from another US invasion after the Bay of Pigs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a valid reason, for example: To protect Cuba, a communist ally, from another US invasion after the Bay of Pigs. To gain a bargaining position, possibly over Berlin. [1]
